summary: Convert a sentinel value to a missing value.
documentation: NULLIF compares its two arguments and returns NULL when they are equal. Otherwise it returns the first argument. It is useful when an existing storage convention uses a special value to represent missing data.
returns: NULL if equal, otherwise the first expression.
caution: NULLIF does not trim or normalize values. Only convert a sentinel after confirming it cannot be a legitimate value.
scenarios: Convert blank imported phone values into missing data.
Normalize a legacy unknown-value marker in a report.
Protect a reporting denominator by converting zero to NULL.
title: Normalize blank phone fields
problem: From contacts(id INTEGER, phone TEXT), return id and NULLIF(phone, '') as phone. Empty strings become NULL; preserve whitespace-only strings and existing NULL. Order by id.
goal: Use NULLIF() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Compare phone with the empty string; do not trim it.
